title: Pharma water system services, URS to service | Aquemi
meta: Design, fabrication, FAT/SAT, IQ/OQ/PQ, service and upgrades for PW, WFI and pure steam, on one traceability record from URS on, per EU GMP Annex 15.
eyebrow: SERVICES · URS TO THE LAST SERVICE VISIT · EU GMP ANNEX 15 · ASTM E2500 · GAMP 5
headline: One team and one traceable record, from your URS to the last service visit
lead: EU GMP Annex 15, 3.2 makes the user requirement specification (URS) the point of reference throughout the validation lifecycle. That reference usually breaks at the hand-offs: a designer, a fabricator, a qualification contractor and a service company, each with their own documents. We carry your Purified Water (PW), Water for Injection (WFI) or pure steam system through design, fabrication, factory and site acceptance testing (FAT and SAT), installation, operational and performance qualification (IQ, OQ, PQ) and service on one traceability matrix, so every requirement keeps the test that proves it and every later change shows what it touches. Tell us where your project stands and we start there.

blocks.h: Qualification evidence is lost between suppliers, not inside them
body: Each stage of a water system produces evidence the next one depends on. IQ verifies the installation against the approved P&IDs (Annex 15, 3.9). FAT results stand in for IQ/OQ tests only where the protocol was written to be leveraged and transport and installation cannot affect the function (Annex 15, 3.6). PQ alert levels come from data on a system whose design intent is known. Service keeps that state only if every part fitted and every calibration traces back to the qualified design, and every change goes through change control (Annex 15, section 11).

When four companies hold four sets of documents, your validation team becomes the integrator: reconciling tag numbers, repeating tests already run at the factory because the protocol was not approved in time, rebuilding a dead leg register at IQ. We write each document from the one before it, against the same requirement IDs, and send drafts at each stage so your quality unit reviews as we go rather than at the end.
Each service can also be bought alone. When we join a project part way, we tell you at the start what we need from the parties before us for the record to hold together.

blocks.h: The lifecycle we carry, on one traceability matrix
blocks.caption: Each requirement in your URS gets an ID at the first review. The same ID appears in the functional specification, on the P&IDs, in the FAT, SAT, IQ and OQ test cases and in the PQ sampling plan, and is the reference when a service visit or an upgrade changes the system. An upgrade re-enters the lifecycle at design, with its requalification scope stated first.

blocks.h: One requirement, followed from URS to year five of service
cols: URS-012: Purified Water conductivity ≤ 1.3 µS/cm at 25 °C at every point of use (USP <645> stage 1)
rows: URS review
Accepted as testable. Linked to the generator outlet guarantee of [outlet conductivity guarantee, µS/cm @ 25 °C] and to loop return monitoring.
Design

Functional specification clause: water above the divert setpoint, set below your alert level, goes to drain until it recovers. Conductivity sensors and the divert valve marked as critical design elements in the risk assessment.
Fabrication
Sensor tees welded, numbered on the weld map, borescoped and listed in the dead leg register at L/D ≤ 2.
FAT
Divert tested at setpoint with a simulated signal; sensor calibration certificates checked; test case flagged for leverage at OQ.
SAT and OQ
Conductivity on your feed water, read on the raw, non-temperature-compensated value, at peak draw and after sanitization.
PQ
Conductivity at every point of use through three phases and at least 12 months; alert level set from your data, inside the 1.3 µS/cm limit.
Service

Cell constant verified to within ± 2 % at each calibration (USP <645>) and the as-found value recorded. An out-of-tolerance as-found is written up for your quality system, with the release decisions it may affect.
Upgrade
A new generation step re-opens this line of the matrix: what the change can affect, what is retested, and how long sampling runs before release.

Service plans with a stated response time per fault severity, calibration to USP <645> and <643>, like-for-like spares and reports fit for your GMP records. First step: a service plan quote.
RO/EDI conversions, sanitization changes, online TOC and Part 11 controls on systems from any builder, with the requalification scope known before the first cut. First step: a system assessment.

blocks.h: Questions engineering, validation and quality teams ask

items.q: Can the company that builds the system also qualify it?
items.a: Yes, under your control. Annex 15, 2.6 asks that protocols and documents supplied by a third party are confirmed by your own personnel as suitable and compliant with your procedures before approval. Your quality unit approves every protocol before execution and every report after it; we write and execute. If your procedures call for an independent qualification contractor, we hand them the traceability matrix and FAT and commissioning records written to be leveraged.

items.q: Do we have to use your document templates?
items.a: No. We write IQ, OQ and PQ documents in your templates where you have them, and keep our requirement IDs inside them so the trace survives. Where you have none, we use ours, and your quality unit approves the templates once, at the start.

items.q: How long from URS to water released for use?
items.a: It depends on scope and your approval cycles. For a packaged PW skid, plan on [design to DQ, weeks] for design, [approved design to FAT, weeks] to FAT and [IQ/OQ on site, days] on site for IQ and OQ. PQ then needs at least two phases of two weeks each; water may be used for manufacturing during phase 2 if the data show the required quality and your quality unit approves it (WHO TRS 1033 Annex 3, 11.3). We give you a dated schedule with the proposal.

items.q: Who is our contact across the stages?
items.a: [Confirm: one named project engineer from URS review to handover, and how the system passes to the service team.] The traceability matrix and the turnover package go with the system, so the service engineer starts from the same record as the project team.

items.q: Can we buy one stage only?
items.a: Yes. Each service has its own first step and its own documents. The table above shows what we need when we join part way.

items.a: [Confirm any-builder scope and the equipment types covered.] We start with an assessment or a condition survey, because a quote without the as-built state and a year of data either carries contingency or leaves the validation to be found during the work. Send it as a proposal request: the service request form is for systems already registered with us.
[Provinces and regions served for projects, and service bases with their coverage area.] The response times in each service plan are stated for that coverage area.
